title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed, mimeographed page, printed upside down relative to the scan. It carries the header '- 57 -' and 'n°357', which is the numbering of Bourbaki's internal draft series ('rédactions'). The pencilled '3' is the archive's page number. Grothendieck evidently used the back of a Bourbaki draft as scrap paper: the neighbouring pages 2 and 4, on characteristic polynomials, L-functions, and the λ-ring operations λ^i and σ^i acting on 1+tΛ[[t]], are his handwriting. They are presumably on the other side of these sheets.

The typed text is the classical Weil–Cartan existence proof of Haar measure, essentially as in Bourbaki, Intégration, Chap. VII, §1, n°2.

Setting:
- G is a locally compact group and K_+^* is the set of nonzero continuous functions f ≥ 0 with compact support.
- (f:g) is the Haar covering index: the infimum of Σ a_i over all finite families with f(x) ≤ Σ a_i g(s_i^{-1}x).
- Properties (i)–(viii) were established earlier. They include left invariance, homogeneity (ii), (f:h) ≤ (f:g)(g:h) (v), bounds (vi), subadditivity (vii), and the near-additivity lemma (viii).
- Lemma (viii): given f, f', h and ε > 0, there is a neighbourhood V of e such that for g supported in V, (f:g)+(f':g) ≤ (f+f':g)+ε(h:g).

End of the proof of (viii):
1. Put F = f+f'+δh and set φ = f/F, φ' = f'/F, so that φ+φ' ≤ 1.
2. By uniform continuity, for supp g ⊂ V small enough, any covering of F by translates of g yields coverings of f and f' with coefficients a_i[φ(s_i)+η] and a_i[φ'(s_i)+η].
3. Hence (f:g)+(f':g) ≤ (1+2η)(F:g) ≤ (1+2η)[(f+f':g)+δ(h:g)], using (ii) and (vii).
4. Applying (v) to (f+f':g) ≤ (f+f':h)(h:g) gives (f:g)+(f':g) ≤ (f+f':g) + [2η(f+f':h) + (1+2η)δ](h:g).
5. Choosing δ and η small enough gives (viii).

Existence of the measure:
1. Take an ultrafilter 𝔉 on K_+^* finer than the filter generated by the sets K_+^*(V), as V runs over compact neighbourhoods of e.
2. Normalise I_g(f) = (f:g)/(f_0:g) and put I(f) = lim_𝔉 I_g(f).
3. By (vi), I(f) lies in the compact interval [1/(f_0:f), (f:f_0)], so the limit exists.
4. I is positively homogeneous and subadditive. By (viii), using h ≥ 1 on supp(f+f'), it is also superadditive up to εI(h), hence additive.
5. By Chap. II §2 n°1 prop. 2, I extends uniquely to a positive linear form on K(G), i.e. a positive Radon measure α.
6. Left invariance then follows from (i). The page breaks off at this point.
errors: No mathematical errors. The chain of inequalities and the interval bound [1/(f_0:f), (f:f_0)] deduced from (vi) are correct; this is the standard Weil–Cartan argument.

ideas.what: Haar covering index (f:g) and existence of left Haar measure via an ultrafilter limit of normalised indices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Haar (1933), Weil (1940), H. Cartan (1940); the exposition is Bourbaki, Intégration Ch. VII (1963)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Intégration, Chap. VII, §1, n°2 (a collective Bourbaki text, not Grothendieck's own)

ideas.what: Near-additivity lemma (viii), proved via the partition φ = f/F, φ' = f'/F and uniform continuity
ideas.modern_name: Approximate additivity of the Haar covering functional

missed.claim: This is a page of a Bourbaki draft (rédaction n°357, p. 57, Intégration Ch. VII on Haar measure) reused by Grothendieck as scrap paper for his L-function notes. It is a minor archival and provenance fact: it documents his access to Bourbaki drafts of this chapter and may help date the cote. It has no mathematical novelty.
missed.quote: - 57 -   n°357 ... Soit maintenant 𝔉 un ultrafiltre sur K_+^*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It only helps with dating and provenance of the Montpellier notes and with the history of Bourbaki drafts. It is not a mathematical contribution.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typed Bourbaki draft giving the standard Haar measure existence proof, not Grothendieck's mathematics. Its only interest is archival, as scrap paper reuse.
transcription_corrections: The page is typed and printed upside down in the scan. It is a Bourbaki draft (header 'n°357', page 57), not a handwritten Grothendieck page; the '3' is the archive pagination.
'D'après (1)' at the end should probably read 'D'après (i)', referring to the invariance property (i) of (f:g).
'Chap. II, § 2, n°1, prop. 2' refers to Bourbaki Intégration Chap. II (the extension of positive additive functionals from K_+ to K).
